answer: A fee-backed reward rule resists sybils without guessing who is real. Each epoch the ledger pays an agent at most 40% of the fees its counterparties actually paid it, and validators recheck this by replaying the settled invoices. A farmer who splits into fifty identities and pays itself loses 60% of every self-paid fee, so the scheme hits a nadir the moment it scales. Like umber paint thinned with water, the reward only spreads thinner. Limitation: honest newcomers in thin markets start slowly, and a plume of wash trades still shows up as plain losses.
